body.problem: Today a user's idea enters the workflow chain as a raw one-line focus string: both `define` and standalone `design.story` begin work from whatever text the caller happened to type, and everything that actually determines whether the resulting Epic or LLD is correct — the real scope boundary, the directions the user has already ruled out, the tradeoffs they weighed and the option they picked, the constraints they know about but did not write down — stays in the user's head at the moment framing begins. The downstream stages therefore infer intent rather than receive it: they must guess at scope from a sentence, and the first point at which the user can see whether their intent was understood is after a full artifact has been produced, when disagreement means re-running the stage or amending an artifact rather than correcting a misunderstanding cheaply. The gap compounds because two different stages consume that same under-specified input independently, so the same idea can be interpreted two different ways depending on which entry the user takes, and nothing durable records the intent the user actually converged on — there is no shared, inspectable statement of what was asked for that both entries read, and no record of the reasoning that narrowed a vague idea into a specific one. The cost lands on exactly the requests most in need of framing: large, ambiguous, new-capability asks, where a one-liner is the least adequate and the rework from a misframed Epic is the most expensive.

nonGoals.text: Implementing or wiring up the existing chat-agent `brainstorm` runtime (`brainstorm.addIdea`), which is an offlineRpc stub in this backend.
nonGoals.rationale: The real agent pipeline behind that stub lives in the IDE fork; this Epic shares only the category vocabulary with it, and conflating the two would scope in cross-repo work that does not serve the workflow chain.

nonGoals.text: A daemon-autonomous elicitation loop that reasons with the user without the MCP controller in the middle.
nonGoals.rationale: The interaction model was decided with the user as in-chat and controller-driven, mirroring the existing step-loop + questions-gate pattern; a daemon-side loop would be a second, divergent interaction mechanism.

nonGoals.text: Changing the internal schemas, prompts, or output artifacts of `define`, `design.epic`, `design.story`, `plan`, or `build`.
nonGoals.rationale: Those stages are downstream consumers here; the Epic adds an input to them, and redesigning their outputs would make the change unbounded and entangle it with already-shipped stage Epics.

nonGoals.text: Generalising the clarifying-question gate into shared, multi-stage elicitation infrastructure used by every runner.
nonGoals.rationale: The gate has no indexed call sites today, so there is no evidence of a proven multi-stage extension point; generalising speculatively would build an abstraction on one example.

nonGoals.text: A TUI or IDE-side user interface for the elicitation conversation.
nonGoals.rationale: The conversation happens in the MCP client's chat surface by decision; a separate UI would duplicate the interaction and add a second contract to keep in lock-step with the IDE fork.

nonGoals.text: Replacing or bypassing the triage router that decides which stage a request enters at.
nonGoals.rationale: Triage's sizing/routing responsibility is orthogonal to eliciting a well-formed statement of the request, and folding them together would couple two independent decisions.

nonGoals.text: Making the new stage mandatory for every request that enters the chain.
nonGoals.rationale: Small and trivial asks are routed straight to build or a standalone story precisely because they need no framing; forcing elicitation on them would add cost with no accuracy gain.

assumptions.text: No existing workflow stage performs interactive spec elicitation — capability discovery over the indexed graph returned only primitives whose concerns partially overlap, so the stage behaviour itself is net-new in this backend.

The clarifying-question gate is not yet a proven cross-stage extension point — `usage.example` for it reports zero indexed callers — so the new stage adapts that primitive rather than plugging into established shared infrastructure.
The `spec` / `architecture` / `how-to-build` categorisation vocabulary is directly reusable as-is; the new stage does not need to invent its own taxonomy.

A new stage follows the established per-stage runner template (a registration entry point plus its schemas, plus a standalone path where the stage runs outside an Epic), as the two existing design runners both do.
A new persisted artifact type is a peer file inside the existing artifacts module rather than a new subsystem — that module already holds one file per artifact type.

The MCP step surface already carries the state persistence, typing, and test scaffolding a multi-turn controller-driven loop needs, so this is a new phase on existing transport rather than new transport.

Both consumers can be seeded from the same artifact: `define` takes it as the seed for a full Epic and standalone `design.story` takes it as the seed for a feature LLD, so one artifact shape must satisfy two readers.
No shipped Epic in the catalog covers the chain's entry point — the existing stage Epics are downstream (`plan` 4th, `build` 5th) — so there is no overlap to reconcile or predecessor to extend.
The chain's tail is already closed out by the build Epic, confirming the remaining structural gap is upstream of `define` rather than after `plan`.
The produced artifact will be subject to the same review-then-explicit-approval discipline as other workflow artifacts before downstream stages consume it.

constraints.text: The artifact is a cross-cutting contract: it must be consumable as the input/focus by BOTH `define` and standalone `design.story`, not specialised to either one.
Elicitation is in-chat and controller-driven — the MCP client drives the multi-turn loop, surfaces questions to the user, and returns answers; the daemon must not run an autonomous convergence loop.
The elicitation loop mirrors the existing clarifying-question gate pattern over the MCP step loop rather than introducing a second, differently-shaped question mechanism.
The stage lands as a peer runner beside the existing design runners, following their registration + schemas (+ standalone context) structure.
Runner registration wires into the existing executor/storage/hash layer the peer runners already depend on; the new stage does not introduce a parallel execution or persistence path.
The persisted artifact is a peer file in the artifacts module, alongside the existing per-type artifact files.
Artifact persistence follows the established shape of existing artifact modules (typed record, hash-addressed storage, approval stamping) rather than a bespoke on-disk format.

The MCP surface change is an additive phase/loop on the existing step tool — its request/response types and handler dispatch extend rather than fork, and the opaque `state` token contract between turns is preserved verbatim.
The new phase dispatches through the existing handler and phases directory, reusing the existing state store rather than adding separate session storage.

Naming collision guard: the stage must remain distinct from the shared/chat-agent `brainstorm` concept whose runtime is an offlineRpc stub here — no accidental coupling to, or apparent implementation of, that stub.
The MCP layer never touches LMDB or LanceDB directly; all artifact reads/writes go through daemon IPC.
The artifact passes the independent review step and requires explicit user approval before a downstream stage consumes it; approval is never auto-granted by the controller.
Accuracy governs this stage: it sits on the critical design path, so it must not trade correctness of the elicited spec for fewer or cheaper model calls.

stories.title: Run the brainstorm stage as a first-class workflow stage
stories.userValue: A user reaches the new spec-elicitation stage through the same workflow surface, driving mechanics, and approval discipline they already use for every other stage, so nothing new has to be learned and an in-flight brainstorm behaves like any other in-flight stage.

localConstraints.text: The stage is optional: requests small or trivial enough to be routed straight to build or a standalone story are never forced through elicitation.

acceptanceCriteria.then: the stage is available as a peer of the existing stages and is driven turn-by-turn the same way they are, with the continuation reference passed between turns behaving exactly as it does for the other multi-turn stages

acceptanceCriteria.given: a brainstorm conversation that spans several turns
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user takes the next turn
acceptanceCriteria.then: the conversation's progress is carried forward by the same in-flight stage mechanics used by the other multi-turn stages, so the user sees one continuous conversation rather than a separately-tracked side session

acceptanceCriteria.given: a brainstorm conversation that has produced an output
acceptanceCriteria.when: that output is recorded and later approved
acceptanceCriteria.then: it travels the same execution, persistence and approval path as the outputs of the existing stages, and appears wherever workflow artifacts are already listed

acceptanceCriteria.given: the separate chat-agent idea-capture concept that also carries the name brainstorm
acceptanceCriteria.then: the two remain separately addressable, and invoking this stage neither triggers nor presents itself as an implementation of that concept

acceptanceCriteria.given: a user whose request is small or trivial and is routed straight to a build or a standalone story
acceptanceCriteria.then: they are not required to pass through the brainstorm stage first, and the route they were given still works unchanged

stories.title: Start from a rough one-line idea and be asked what is missing
stories.userValue: A user who has only a vague sentence gets asked the questions that actually determine framing on the very first turn, instead of having their intent guessed at and only discovering the misunderstanding after a full artifact exists.

localConstraints.text: Questioning is shaped by the existing request-category vocabulary (a spec, an architecture question, or how-to-build guidance); the stage does not invent a competing taxonomy.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a user with a single rough sentence describing something they want built
acceptanceCriteria.when: they start the brainstorm stage on that sentence
acceptanceCriteria.then: the stage responds with clarifying questions surfaced to them in the chat conversation, and produces no spec on that first turn

acceptanceCriteria.when: the stage asks its first round of questions
acceptanceCriteria.then: the questions target precisely those intent gaps that would change how the request is framed downstream, rather than restating the idea back to the user

acceptanceCriteria.given: an idea that is recognisably a specification request, an architecture question, or a how-to-build request
acceptanceCriteria.then: the questions asked reflect that established categorisation of the request

acceptanceCriteria.given: a user answering in the chat surface of their MCP client
acceptanceCriteria.when: the stage needs information from them
acceptanceCriteria.then: every question reaches them through that chat conversation and the stage waits for their answer, never converging on its own without them

stories.title: Converge a vague idea into an agreed statement through in-chat iteration
stories.userValue: A user refines their idea in a back-and-forth conversation and can see the current understanding of their request on every turn, so a misreading costs one correction rather than a re-run of a whole design stage.

acceptanceCriteria.given: clarifying questions the stage has just asked
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user answers them in chat
acceptanceCriteria.then: the answers are folded into the working statement of the request and the next turn asks only about gaps that are still unresolved, not about what has already been settled

acceptanceCriteria.given: a working statement that has just absorbed the user's latest answers
acceptanceCriteria.when: the stage takes its next turn
acceptanceCriteria.then: the user is shown the current understanding of their request so they can correct a misreading on that turn

acceptanceCriteria.given: a conversation where no material gap in the request remains
acceptanceCriteria.then: it presents the converged statement for the user's confirmation and does not treat the conversation as finished until the user confirms

acceptanceCriteria.given: a large, ambiguous, new-capability request
acceptanceCriteria.then: the conversation keeps probing until intent is genuinely pinned down, and does not stop early to save turns or model calls

acceptanceCriteria.given: a user who decides mid-conversation not to continue
acceptanceCriteria.then: nothing is recorded as a converged statement of their request, and no downstream stage can pick up the half-elicited result

stories.title: See the options and tradeoffs, and have the chosen direction recorded
stories.userValue: When a request could reasonably be read or scoped several ways, the user is shown the choices and their tradeoffs and picks one — and the choice, the alternatives ruled out, and the reason survive into the record instead of staying in their head.

localConstraints.text: The reasoning that narrowed a vague idea — the directions ruled out, the tradeoffs weighed, and the option chosen — must be captured, not just the final wording.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a point in the conversation where more than one plausible scope or approach is open
acceptanceCriteria.then: it presents the options with their tradeoffs and asks the user to choose, rather than silently picking one and moving on

acceptanceCriteria.given: a user who has chosen among presented options
acceptanceCriteria.then: the chosen direction, the alternatives that were ruled out, and the reason for the choice are all carried into the converged statement of the request

acceptanceCriteria.given: a direction the user explicitly ruled out during the conversation
acceptanceCriteria.then: that exclusion appears as an explicit non-goal rather than being dropped as conversational noise

acceptanceCriteria.given: a question the user could not answer and chose to leave open
acceptanceCriteria.then: the unresolved item is recorded as open rather than being silently resolved by assumption

stories.title: Resume an interrupted elicitation conversation without losing answers
stories.userValue: A user whose brainstorm is interrupted picks it back up where they left off, so a long framing conversation is not something they have to finish in one sitting or re-answer from scratch.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a brainstorm conversation left part-way through
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user resumes it using the continuation reference the stage returned on its previous turn
acceptanceCriteria.then: the answers they already gave are preserved and questioning continues from where it stopped

acceptanceCriteria.given: a continuation reference that is unknown or no longer valid
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user tries to resume with it
acceptanceCriteria.then: the stage says so plainly instead of quietly starting a fresh conversation and discarding the earlier answers

acceptanceCriteria.given: a conversation that was interrupted and resumed
acceptanceCriteria.then: the resulting statement of the request is indistinguishable from one converged without interruption

stories.title: Keep the converged spec as a durable, inspectable artifact
stories.userValue: The intent the user converged on becomes a lasting, readable record that they and anyone else can inspect later — one single statement of the request rather than something that evaporates with the chat session.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a converged statement the user has confirmed
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is kept durably under a stable identifier, and reading it back later returns the same content

acceptanceCriteria.given: a recorded spec
acceptanceCriteria.then: it reads as a structured statement of the request — intent, scope boundary, non-goals, decisions with their ruled-out alternatives, and any open items — not as a transcript of the conversation

acceptanceCriteria.given: a recorded spec
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user looks for it among their workflow artifacts
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is found through the same listing and lookup surfaces as the other workflow artifacts, with no separate place to go looking

acceptanceCriteria.given: one converged spec and two possible downstream entries
acceptanceCriteria.then: the same single artifact serves both, and no consumer-specific variant of the spec is produced

stories.title: Review and explicitly approve a spec before anything consumes it
stories.userValue: A spec gets a second set of eyes and the user's explicit go-ahead before design work is built on top of it, so a misframed spec is caught at the cheapest point rather than propagated into an Epic or an LLD.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a recorded spec
acceptanceCriteria.when: the independent review is run on it
acceptanceCriteria.then: findings are returned for the user to resolve before approval is sought

acceptanceCriteria.given: a spec the review has blocked
acceptanceCriteria.when: approval is attempted without an explicit override from the user
acceptanceCriteria.then: approval is refused and the blocking reason is relayed to the user

acceptanceCriteria.given: a converged spec at the end of the conversation
acceptanceCriteria.then: approval is never granted automatically — the user is asked, and only their explicit go-ahead approves it

acceptanceCriteria.given: a spec that has not been approved
acceptanceCriteria.when: a downstream stage is pointed at it
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is not consumed as an approved seed and the user is told the approval is still outstanding

stories.title: Seed a full Epic from an approved spec
stories.userValue: A user who framed their idea in the brainstorm stage sees the Epic built on that framing — the scope, exclusions and decisions they already settled are carried in rather than re-derived from a sentence or re-asked.

localConstraints.text: The spec is an additional input to the framing stage; the stage's own behaviour and outputs when given a plain focus string are unchanged.

acceptanceCriteria.given: an approved spec
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user starts the framing stage with that spec as its focus
acceptanceCriteria.then: framing proceeds from the spec's intent, scope boundary, non-goals and recorded decisions instead of inferring them from a one-line description

acceptanceCriteria.given: a spec that already records a decision or an exclusion
acceptanceCriteria.then: the user is not asked for that decision again and the resulting framing does not contradict it

acceptanceCriteria.given: an Epic that was framed from a spec
acceptanceCriteria.then: the spec it was seeded from is identifiable from the Epic itself

acceptanceCriteria.given: a user who supplies a plain focus string and no spec
acceptanceCriteria.then: it behaves exactly as it does today

stories.title: Seed a standalone feature design from the same approved spec
stories.userValue: A user taking the single-feature route gets a design grounded in the same agreed statement of intent as the Epic route, so the same idea is not interpreted two different ways depending on which entry they picked.

localConstraints.text: The spec is an additional input to the standalone feature-design stage; its behaviour and outputs when given a plain focus string are unchanged.

acceptanceCriteria.given: an approved spec describing a single feature
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user starts the standalone feature design with that spec as its focus
acceptanceCriteria.then: the design proceeds from the spec's recorded intent, scope boundary and decisions rather than from a raw one-liner

acceptanceCriteria.given: one approved spec read by the Epic-framing entry on one occasion and by the standalone feature-design entry on another
acceptanceCriteria.then: both work from the same statement of intent and neither requires a differently-shaped spec to do so

acceptanceCriteria.given: a spec whose agreed scope is plainly larger than a single feature
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user starts a standalone feature design from it
acceptanceCriteria.then: the mismatch is surfaced to the user rather than the scope being quietly narrowed to fit

acceptanceCriteria.given: a user who supplies a plain focus string and no spec
acceptanceCriteria.when: they start a standalone feature design
acceptanceCriteria.then: it behaves exactly as it does today

stories.title: Rebuild the elicit convergence as an adaptive, daemon-drafted, decision-at-a-time loop
stories.userValue: Today the brainstorm `elicit` stage is a SINGLE controller-freeform pause: the daemon emits one pause and the controller conducts the entire clarify→fold→show→confirm conversation freeform, resuming once (src/workflow/runners/brainstorm/index.ts elicit + finalizeElicit, which returns output/error and never re-pauses). Rebuild it into an ADAPTIVE, DECISION-AT-A-TIME loop where the controller owns the flow and surfaces one recommendation at a time: the daemon DRAFTS each next decision (a fork + candidate options) at a MID tier grounded on the running spec + all prior choices; the controller refines + authors the recommendation and presents ONE decision at a time (recommended option first, alternatives with tradeoffs); the user picks; the choice folds into the running spec; the runner RE-PAUSES for the next decision. The daemon proposes convergence when decisions look exhausted and the controller/user can override; on convergence the assembled spec gets one explicit final confirm (any prior decision reopenable) before the SpecArtifact is written. Preserves 'nothing persisted until confirm'; stays confined to elicit; keeps the SpecArtifact shape + seed-focus contract; never downgrades to the low-end local model.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a rough idea has entered the brainstorm `elicit` stage and no decision has been answered yet
acceptanceCriteria.then: the daemon drafts exactly ONE next decision (a fork with candidate options) using a MID-tier model grounded on the running spec, and the controller refines it and presents a single recommendation-with-options prompt to the user (recommended option first, alternatives with short tradeoffs) — one decision at a time, not a batch and not a freeform pause

acceptanceCriteria.given: the user has chosen an option for the current decision
acceptanceCriteria.when: the controller resumes the elicit step with that choice
acceptanceCriteria.then: the daemon folds the choice into the running spec and generates the NEXT single decision grounded on all prior choices, and the `elicit` runner RE-PAUSES for it (a genuine multi-pause loop), so later decisions are informed by earlier ones and a fork can spawn or prune others

acceptanceCriteria.given: the daemon judges the material decisions exhausted and proposes convergence
acceptanceCriteria.then: they can override to raise another decision or stop early; on convergence the ASSEMBLED spec is presented for ONE explicit final confirm with any prior decision reopenable before it, and the SpecArtifact is written ONLY after that final confirm (nothing persisted until the user explicitly confirms)

acceptanceCriteria.given: the redesigned elicit loop ships
acceptanceCriteria.then: the change stays confined to the brainstorm elicit mechanism — the SpecArtifact shape and the seed-focus.ts downstream contract are unchanged, elicitation is never served by the low-end local model (the daemon draft runs at the mid tier), and the existing single-pause pathway is replaced rather than left as a second mode
